title: Black Week and Christmas: Planning Outdoor Advertising in Q4
excerpt: Q4 is the busiest time of the year. How to plan an outdoor campaign for Black Week and Christmas so you are visible before customers decide.
content:
# Black Week and Christmas: Planning Outdoor Advertising in Q4

From Black Week at the end of November until Christmas, cities are full of people shopping, looking for gifts and visiting Christmas markets. It is also the time when online visibility is most expensive, because everyone advertises at once. Outdoor advertising is one of the few media where your surface is yours alone for the whole campaign.

Here is how to plan your Q4 campaign.

## The key dates in 2026

- **Black Friday:** Friday, 27 November 2026 (calendar week 48)
- **Black Week:** the week around Black Friday, i.e. calendar week 48
- **Cyber Monday:** Monday, 30 November 2026 (calendar week 49)
- **Advent and the Christmas season:** late November to Christmas Eve on 24 December 2026 (calendar week 52)

In Basel, the autumn fair and the Christmas market also shape the second half of the year and bring many people into the city centre.

## Book early

The best surfaces are in especially high demand in Q4. Our own sites show it: Riehenring 141 is currently booked by Grand Casino Basel, and Riehenring 70 is taken for calendar weeks 44–47 of 2026. If you want to be visible in the Christmas season, plan early, for this year and for next.

The minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks. A period from calendar week 45 to 48, for example, covers the weeks before Black Week and Black Week itself. If you want to be present until Christmas, plan for longer.

You will find our current surfaces and their availability under [Sites](/en/standorte).

## Be visible before customers decide

Many people decide where to shop in the days before Black Week. A large surface in the city in the preceding weeks builds awareness, so your brand is the one people search for when the offers go live.

Outdoor often works before the search. That is exactly what you need at a time when digital competition is at its fiercest. More on [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix).

## Choose the format for the campaign's rhythm

**A large scaffolding site for a big impact.** For Black Week or a launch in the Christmas season, a large scaffolding surface delivers a message nobody misses. One example is the «Sparkling Life» campaign by [Grand Casino Basel at Riehenring 141](/en/cases/grand-casino-basel-riehenring), where two banners cover both street faces of a corner building right by Messe Basel.

**A facade for the whole season.** If you want to be present from November to Christmas, a facade builds awareness week after week.

**Both combined.** A facade provides the base presence, and a scaffolding surface adds an extra accent around Black Week.

## Keep the message simple

In Q4, advertising messages easily drown each other out. One big image, few words and your logo work better than a list of offers. Do not print discounts that might change during the campaign. Say what people should remember: who you are and where to find you.

A banner stays up for several weeks, so design it to work from the run-up to Christmas through to the holidays. See our [creative best practices](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung) and the article on [print files for scaffolding banners](/en/blog/geruestbanner-druckdaten-spezifikationen-gestaltung) for design tips.

## Align with your digital channels

Use the same visual and the same key message outdoors and online. Someone who saw your banner on the way to work should recognise your ad online immediately. Ideally, start the outdoor campaign before the digital promotions, so awareness is already there when the offers go live.

## Measure the campaign

Track searches for your brand, visits to your website and visits to stores near the sites, and compare them with a period without the campaign. More in [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen).

## A Q4 checklist

1. Set the dates: Black Week, the Christmas season, or both?
2. Book the surface early, for at least four weeks
3. Choose the format: a big impact or presence for the whole season
4. Design a visual that works for the whole period
5. Deliver print files in good time
6. Align with your digital campaigns
7. Agree on measurement before launch

## FAQ

### When should I book outdoor advertising for Christmas?

As early as possible. The best surfaces are in high demand in Q4. Also allow time for design, print files and, where needed, the permit. [From booking to banner](/en/blog/zeitplan-ooh-kampagne-buchung-bis-banner) shows what a realistic timeline looks like.

### When is Black Friday 2026?

On Friday, 27 November 2026, in calendar week 48.

### Is outdoor advertising worth it during Black Week?

Yes, especially in the weeks before. Outdoor builds awareness before the offers go live, and your surface is yours alone for the whole campaign.

Planning your Q4 campaign, or want to secure surfaces for 2027? [Contact us](/en/contact).

title: Employer Branding with Outdoor Advertising: Reach Talent Where They Are
excerpt: The best candidates are often not actively looking. How to use outdoor advertising to build your employer brand and reach talent in Basel and the region.
content:
# Employer Branding with Outdoor Advertising: Reach Talent Where They Are

Many of the people you would like to hire are not looking for a new job right now. They do not read job ads or visit careers pages. But they move through the city every day, on the way to work, to their studies or back home. That is where outdoor advertising comes in: you become known as an employer before anyone even starts looking.

## Why outdoor advertising works for employer branding

### You reach people in their daily lives

Choose sites on the routes your future employees take every day: commuter routes, tram lines, the area around universities and vocational schools. That way you meet your audience again and again, without them having to search.

### Size builds trust

A large advertising surface in the city shows that a company is present and has plans. That matters when someone is considering a move. An employer people already know seems more trustworthy than one they read about for the first time in a job ad.

### Your own employees see it too

A campaign in the cityscape gets seen, shared and talked about, inside the company too. Employees who see their employer in large format in the city talk about it. That makes them ambassadors.

## Particularly relevant in Basel

Basel has some particular features for employer branding:

- **Cross-border commuters:** many people commute into the city every day from France and Germany. If you are looking for skilled people from the region, you reach them on the commuter routes.
- **Trade fairs and congresses:** professionals from around the world regularly gather around Messe Basel and the Congress Center.
- **Strong industries:** Basel is a major location for life sciences, logistics and services. Competition for talent is correspondingly high.

A site like [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141), on one of the busiest routes from the motorway and right by Messe Basel, delivers 39'851 contacts per day, many of them commuters.

## What the message should look like

A job ad does not belong on scaffolding. A large format needs a clear statement:

- **One reason why people should work for you.** Not a list of benefits.
- **Real images**, ideally of your own people.
- **A clear sender:** your logo, large and clearly visible.
- **A simple next step:** a short, memorable web address. A QR code pays off mainly where people stand still, such as at a tram stop.

Read more about design in our [creative best practices](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung).

## Choose the right format

- **Scaffolding advertising** suits a big recruitment drive, for example when you open a new location or need to fill many positions at once. More under [scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding).
- **Facade advertising** fits when employer branding is an ongoing effort and you want to be present for months. More under [facade advertising](/en/facade).
- **Apprenticeship marketing:** if you are looking for apprentices, plan the campaign ahead of the period when young people choose an apprenticeship, and pick sites on the routes to schools.

## Connect with other channels

Outdoor creates awareness; the application happens online. Make sure your careers page, social media channels and job ads use the same message and the same images as the campaign. Someone who has seen your banner and then looks you up should recognise you immediately. More on [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix).

## Measure the impact

During the campaign, track:

- visits to your careers page, especially direct traffic and traffic from the region
- the number of applications compared with a period without the campaign
- searches for your company as an employer

And ask in interviews where candidates first noticed you. It often gives the clearest answer. More methods in [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen).

## FAQ

### Is outdoor advertising suitable for recruitment?

Yes, especially for employer branding. Outdoor reaches people who are not actively looking and makes your company known as an employer. The application itself then runs through your careers page.

### What belongs on an employer branding banner?

A clear statement of why people should work for you, a real image, your logo and a short web address. No list of vacancies.

### How long should an employer branding campaign run?

Long enough for your audience to see the message several times. The minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks. For ongoing employer branding, longer periods make sense.

Want to become more visible as an employer? Tell us who you want to reach, and we will suggest suitable [sites](/en/standorte). [Contact us](/en/contact).

title: Scaffolding Banners: Print Files, Specifications and Design That Works
excerpt: How to prepare print-ready files for a scaffolding banner: file format, resolution, safe zones, mesh, and design that reads from 50 metres away.
content:
# Scaffolding Banners: Print Files, Specifications and Design That Works

A scaffolding banner is often well over a hundred square metres and is seen from a long way off. That places different demands on the print files than an ad on a screen or a poster. Here is what you need to know before your visual goes to print.

For every site we send you the exact dimensions and specifications. This guide gives you the overview.

## File format

- **A vector PDF is the best choice.** Text and logo stay sharp at any size.
- **Convert fonts to outlines** or embed them fully, so nothing shifts at the printer.
- **Colours in CMYK**, not RGB. If your brand uses specific spot colours, provide the colour values so they can be matched as closely as possible in print.
- **Deliver at the scale we specify.** Large-format files are often set up at a reduced scale to keep them manageable. We tell you the right scale for your surface.

## Resolution

A scaffolding banner is viewed from a distance. The resolution needed at final size is therefore much lower than for a print you hold in your hand. Even so, the source image must be sharp and large enough. A small image from the internet looks grainy and blurred across a hundred square metres. Use original photos at full resolution.

## Aspect ratio

Scaffolding surfaces often have unusual proportions, such as very wide or very tall formats. An existing poster design can rarely be used one-to-one. Plan the visual from the start for the specific aspect ratio of the surface.

## Safe zones

The banner is fixed to the scaffolding all the way around. Keep text and logo well away from the edges so nothing disappears behind scaffolding tubes, fixings or edges. Depending on the scaffolding, elements such as passageways or structural parts within the surface may also need to be taken into account. We give you the safe zones for every site.

## Mesh or solid material

Many scaffolding banners are printed on mesh, a fabric with small openings that lets the wind through. That matters for large surfaces on scaffolding. Mesh affects the design:

- Colours look slightly lighter, because light and background show through the openings.
- Very fine details and thin fonts lose sharpness.
- Strong colours and clear shapes work best.

We agree with you before production which material is used for your surface.

## Design that works from a distance

The technical data is one side; the design is the other. What works:

- **Few words.** People drive past and have only a few seconds.
- **Strong contrast** between text and background.
- **One image** rather than several small ones.
- **A big logo.** Make it bigger than you think.
- **Bold typefaces** rather than thin or decorative ones.

Test the visual by looking at it small on your phone. If it is legible there, it will be legible on the scaffolding. More in our [creative best practices for outdoor advertising](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung).

## Think about the site

How is your surface seen? Head-on from a square, at an angle from a main road, or on a corner from two directions? That decides where the key message should go.

At [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141) in Basel, for example, the surface is on a corner building. Grand Casino Basel uses two banners there to cover both street faces. At a site like this, it pays to design the visual so it is recognised on both sides. More in the [Grand Casino Basel case study](/en/cases/grand-casino-basel-riehenring).

## Approval

Because Hyde Media handles the print, we review the files with you before production. Allow time for corrections in case format or resolution needs adjusting. The earlier you know the specifications, the fewer correction rounds you need. [From booking to banner](/en/blog/zeitplan-ooh-kampagne-buchung-bis-banner) shows when each step is due.

## Checklist for your print files

1. Vector PDF in the correct aspect ratio
2. Set up at the specified scale
3. Fonts converted to outlines
4. Colours in CMYK, spot colours specified
5. Images in sufficient original quality
6. Text and logo within the safe zones
7. Visual checked for mesh suitability

## FAQ

### Which file format do I need for a scaffolding banner?

Ideally a vector PDF with fonts converted to outlines and colours in CMYK, at the scale we specify for the surface.

### What resolution does a scaffolding banner need?

At final size, much less than a print for close viewing, because the banner is seen from a distance. The source image must still be sharp and available at original size.

### What is mesh?

A banner material with small openings that lets the wind through. It is often used on scaffolding. Colours look slightly lighter on it, and fine details less sharp.

### Who prints and installs the banner?

Hyde Media handles print, installation, removal and permits. You supply the visual.

Want the specifications for a particular site? [Contact us](/en/contact). See the available surfaces under [scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding).

title: Permits for Scaffolding Advertising in Switzerland: What Advertisers Should Know
excerpt: Who approves scaffolding advertising in Switzerland? An overview of federal law, cantonal responsibilities and the example of Basel-Stadt.
content:
# Permits for Scaffolding Advertising in Switzerland: What Advertisers Should Know

If you want to advertise on scaffolding or a facade in Switzerland, you will almost always need a permit. But which authority is responsible, and which conditions apply, is not regulated uniformly across the country. Alongside federal law, cantonal and municipal rules play a major role.

This article gives a general overview. It is not legal advice, and the rules can change. With Hyde Media you do not have to deal with it yourself anyway: we handle the permit process for scaffolding and facade advertising.

## The framework: federal law

At federal level, the key texts are the Road Traffic Act (SVG) and the Road Signals Ordinance (SSV). Their focus is road safety.

- **Road Traffic Act (Art. 6 SVG):** on roads open to motor vehicles or bicycles, advertising is prohibited if it could be confused with signals or markings, or could otherwise impair road safety, for example by distracting road users.
- **Road Signals Ordinance (SSV):** it regulates roadside advertising in detail. Under the SSV, putting up or changing roadside advertising generally requires a permit from the authority responsible under cantonal law (Art. 99 SSV). Cantons can provide for exceptions.

Roadside advertising here means advertising within drivers' field of view. A large banner at a junction typically falls under it.

## Cantons and municipalities: who is responsible?

Cantonal law determines which authority grants the permit, and the solutions differ considerably. Some examples:

- In the **canton of Lucerne**, the cantonal government has delegated responsibility for advertising permits to the municipalities.
- In the **canton of St. Gallen**, the cantonal police are responsible for advertising on national and cantonal roads.
- In other cantons, municipalities or building authorities decide as part of the building permit process.

On top of that come rules on townscape and landscape protection, heritage conservation and zoning. An advertisement may therefore be unproblematic in traffic terms and still be refused, or approved only with conditions, for townscape reasons.

## Example: Basel-Stadt

In Basel-Stadt, advertising is handled within the building permit process. Applications go to the Building and Hospitality Inspectorate (Bau- und Gastgewerbeinspektorat, BGI). Within the city, design is assessed by the Townscape Commission (Stadtbildkommission). In Riehen and Bettingen, the local townscape commissions take on this role.

The Townscape Commission assesses advertising applications on the basis of the canton's advertising concept (Reklamekonzept). The criteria depend on the location: historic parts of the city call for more restraint than others, and residential areas more than commercial ones.

## Content conditions

A permit can also include conditions on content. An example from our own portfolio: for the scaffolding surface at [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141) in Basel, the city has granted a permit. Alcohol advertising, political advertising and pornographic content are excluded there.

So check early whether your visual fits the conditions of the chosen site. We tell you about them for every site.

## What this means for your planning

### Allow time

The permit process takes time, and the duration varies by authority and application. For sites that already have a permit, this step largely falls away. [From booking to banner](/en/blog/zeitplan-ooh-kampagne-buchung-bis-banner) shows what a realistic timeline looks like.

### Think about the design

Because road safety is a central criterion, visuals should not resemble traffic signals, for example through similar shapes or colours near traffic lights. A clear, calm design is also the better choice in terms of impact.

### Use a partner

For advertisers, permits are rarely the core business. Hyde Media handles the application, coordination with the authorities, and print, installation and removal.

## Sources

The information in this article is based on publicly available sources, including the federal Road Traffic Act (SVG, SR 741.01) and Road Signals Ordinance (SSV, SR 741.21), the canton of Lucerne's guidelines on advertising installations, the St. Gallen cantonal police's information on roadside advertising, and the canton of Basel-Stadt's information on the building permit process for advertising and the Townscape Commission's advertising concept. The current legal text and the practice of the responsible authority are always decisive.

## FAQ

### Does scaffolding advertising in Switzerland need a permit?

Almost always. Under the Road Signals Ordinance, roadside advertising generally requires a permit from the authority responsible under cantonal law. Cantonal and municipal rules come on top.

### Who is responsible for advertising permits in Basel?

In Basel-Stadt, applications go to the Building and Hospitality Inspectorate. Within the city, the Townscape Commission assesses the design on the basis of the advertising concept.

### Do I have to deal with the permit myself?

No. Hyde Media handles the permit process for scaffolding and facade advertising.

### Is there content that is not allowed?

That depends on the permit. At Riehenring 141 in Basel, for example, alcohol advertising, political advertising and pornographic content are excluded.

title: How to Calculate the Reach of an Outdoor Campaign: Contacts, Frequency and Share of Voice
excerpt: Contacts, reach, frequency and share of voice: how to calculate the performance of an outdoor campaign from traffic figures, with an example from Basel.
content:
# How to Calculate the Reach of an Outdoor Campaign: Contacts, Frequency and Share of Voice

Outdoor advertising is measured differently from online advertising. There are no clicks and no cookies, but there are traffic figures. With them you can calculate quite precisely how often your campaign can be seen.

Here are the key terms and a worked example from Basel.

## The four key terms

### Contacts (OTS)

A **contact** is one opportunity for one person to see the ad. The figure is gross: someone who passes five times counts as five contacts. The industry also calls it OTS, "opportunity to see".

### Reach

**Reach** is the number of different people who saw the campaign at least once. It is always lower than the number of contacts, because many people pass several times.

### Frequency

**Frequency** is how often one person saw the campaign on average. Reach × frequency = contacts.

### Share of voice

**Share of voice** describes the share your advertising has of a surface or a market. On digital screens, several advertisers share the airtime, so your share of voice is the share of time your spot runs. With a scaffolding or facade banner you have the surface to yourself: 100 percent of the surface for the whole campaign.

In a broader sense, share of voice is also used for your share of the total advertising pressure in a category. If you are more visible than your competitors, your share of voice is higher.

All the terms are explained briefly in the [glossary](/en/glossar).

## The basic calculation

For a banner the calculation is simple:

**Contacts = contacts per day × 7 × number of weeks**

A banner is up around the clock and not shared with anyone. Everyone who passes has the opportunity to see it.

## An example from Basel

Take our site at [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141), a 175 m² scaffolding surface right next to Messe Basel. The site delivers 39'851 contacts per day.

- **Per week:** 39'851 × 7 = 278'957 contacts
- **Over four weeks** (minimum booking): 278'957 × 4 = 1'115'828 contacts
- **Over eight weeks:** 278'957 × 8 = 2'231'656 contacts

You can run the calculation for other sites and periods yourself in the [campaign calculator](/en/kampagnenrechner).

## From contacts to cost per thousand

To compare sites or media, use the **cost per thousand (CPM)**:

**CPM = campaign cost ÷ contacts × 1,000**

CPM shows what 1,000 contacts cost you. It lets you compare a scaffolding site with a poster network or an online campaign on the same basis. Keep in mind, though, that a contact is not worth the same in every medium. A 175 m² banner that people look at while waiting at the lights works differently from an ad flashing past in a news feed.

## Things to keep in mind

### Contacts are not people

On routes people use every day, many see the same surface again and again. That is a strength, because repetition builds recall. But it means reach is clearly lower than the number of contacts.

### Traffic is not attention

Not everyone who passes looks. A large format, a good site with dwell time and a simple message increase the share of people who actually notice the ad. See our [creative best practices](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung) for design tips.

### Compare like with like

Use contacts to compare sites and plans with each other. When comparing outdoor with other media, calculate CPM the same way for all of them.

## Planning frequency

How often should someone see your message? There is no universal number, but there is a rule of thumb: new or complex messages need more repetition than familiar brands. Longer periods and sites on daily commuter routes increase frequency.

## After the campaign: measure the impact

Traffic figures show how many people could see the campaign. Whether it worked, you measure differently:

- awareness before and after the campaign, for example with a short survey
- searches for your brand during the campaign
- visits to a campaign page or to nearby stores

More in [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen). Read about how outdoor works together with other channels in [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix).

## FAQ

### How do you calculate the contacts of an outdoor campaign?

Contacts per day × 7 × number of weeks. At 39'851 contacts per day, that gives 1'115'828 contacts over four weeks.

### What is the difference between contacts and reach?

Contacts count every opportunity to see the ad, even if the same person passes several times. Reach counts each person only once.

### What does share of voice mean in outdoor advertising?

On digital screens, it is the share of airtime your spot receives. With a banner, you have the surface exclusively. In a broader sense, it is your share of the total advertising pressure in a category.

# Scaffolding Advertising in Basel: How to Choose Site and Format

Basel is a particularly interesting city for scaffolding advertising. It is compact, the tram network is dense, Messe Basel regularly brings in an international audience, and many buildings are being renovated. Whether a campaign works, though, depends mainly on two questions: who do you want to reach, and how do those people move?

Here is a practical guide to choosing site and format.

## Start with movement, not with the surface

The most common mistake is to start with the surface. Ask first how your audience passes the site.

**Drivers** see the surface from a distance and on the move. They have a few seconds. The message must be short and large. At traffic lights, the viewing time gets longer.

**Tram passengers** move more slowly and often sit looking out. At stops, people wait and have time to look.

**Cyclists** are close to the buildings, look ahead and move briskly. They see large banners well but have little time for text.

**Pedestrians** are the slowest and see the surface up close. Here the message can carry a bit more.

The strongest sites in Basel are where several of these groups come together, such as at traffic-light junctions with a tram line.

## What makes a good scaffolding site

### Contacts per day

The most important figure is the number of contacts per day. At Riehenring 141 it is 39'851 contacts per day. Scale the contacts up to the campaign period to compare sites. Our article on [calculating the reach of an outdoor campaign](/en/blog/reichweite-aussenwerbung-berechnen) shows how.

### Visibility from several directions

Corner buildings at junctions are especially valuable because they are seen from several directions. A campaign can cover two street faces there, as Grand Casino Basel does at Riehenring 141 and EVO Fitness did at Burgfelderstrasse.

### Dwell time

Traffic lights, stops and slow traffic extend the time people look at the surface. A site with somewhat less traffic but long dwell time can be more effective than one on a fast road.

### Surroundings and audience

Does the site fit your audience? Around the Messe you reach trade visitors and commuters, in the neighbourhoods the local population, in the city centre people out shopping.

## The key areas in Basel

**Messe Basel and Riehenring.** Traffic converges on the route from the motorway to Messe Basel and the Congress Center. This is where our sites [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141), with 175 m² right next to the Messe, and [Riehenring 70](/en/standorte/riehenring-70), with 125 m² on the way to the Messe, the Congress Center and the Musical Theater Basel, are located. Riehenring 70 is booked for calendar weeks 44–47 of 2026.

**Tram junctions in the neighbourhoods.** Major junctions where trams stop and cars wait at the lights reach commuters and residents alike. One example is the campaign by [EVO Fitness at Burgfelderstrasse 1](/en/cases/evo-fitness-basel-burgfelderstrasse).

**City centre.** Lots of foot traffic, but a sensitive, historic townscape. Large-format advertising is particularly demanding here in terms of design and permits.

For a more detailed overview, see [Top locations for outdoor advertising in Basel](/en/blog/basel-standorte-aussenwerbung).

## Choosing the format

### Size

Larger surfaces stand out more and are visible from further away. What matters, though, is whether your audience can see the surface well. A medium-sized surface at traffic lights can achieve more than a huge one that is only visible at an angle from a moving car.

### One side or two

On corner buildings you can cover both street faces, either with the same visual to strengthen recognition, or with two coordinated visuals.

### Scaffolding or facade

Scaffolding advertising suits campaigns that need high attention in a specific period. For a longer presence, facade advertising is the alternative. See our comparison [Scaffolding vs. facade](/en/blog/geruest-vs-fassade-richtige-wahl).

### Campaign length

The minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks. Longer periods increase repetition and therefore recall.

## Use Basel's calendar

Trade fairs and congresses, the autumn fair, the Advent season and Fasnacht change traffic flows and audiences in the city. If you want to reach fair visitors, plan your campaign around the fair dates. For the Christmas season, early planning pays off; see [Black Week and Christmas](/en/blog/black-week-weihnachten-aussenwerbung-q4).

## Checklist before booking

- Who should see the ad, and how does that audience pass by?
- How many contacts per day does the site offer?
- Is the surface visible from several directions?
- Does the period fit your campaign?
- Does your visual fit the conditions of the permit?
- Can the message be read in the time available?

## FAQ

### Where does scaffolding advertising pay off most in Basel?

At junctions with heavy traffic and tram lines, on main routes such as Riehenring towards Messe Basel, and wherever your audience passes every day.

### Which scaffolding sites does Hyde Media offer in Basel?

You will find a current overview under [Sites](/en/standorte), including Riehenring 141 and Riehenring 70.

### Who takes care of permits, print and installation?

Hyde Media handles print, installation, removal and permits.

Want to start with scaffolding advertising in Basel? [Contact us](/en/contact) for a proposal.

# From Booking to Banner: The Timeline of an OOH Campaign

One of the questions we hear most is not "what does it cost?" but "how fast can we start?". The answer depends on the format, the site and how far along your preparation is. In this article we walk through the steps of a scaffolding or facade advertising campaign, and where things typically get stuck.

## The short version

A campaign goes through six steps: site selection, agreement, design and print files, permit, print and installation. Some of them run in parallel. How much lead time you need depends mainly on two questions: is the visual ready? And is there already a permit for the site?

Our advice: plan generously and work backwards from your start date. The best surfaces are often booked early.

## Step 1: Choose the site

Start with the question of which surface fits the job, not which one happens to be free. Clarify:

- Who do you want to reach, and how does that audience move?
- Which format fits: scaffolding or facade?
- When should the campaign run, and for how long? The minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks.
- How many contacts per day does the site offer?

You will find our available surfaces under [Sites](/en/standorte). Calculate the contacts for different periods in the [campaign calculator](/en/kampagnenrechner).

**Good to know:** scaffolding surfaces only exist while building work is going on. Construction projects follow their own calendar, and the surface becomes available when the scaffolding goes up, not when it suits your media plan. Attractive periods are therefore often booked quickly.

## Step 2: Agreement and specifications

Once the site and period are settled, the booking is agreed. Ask for the exact specifications of the surface straight away: dimensions, aspect ratio, safe zones and file format. Having the right requirements early saves extra work later.

## Step 3: Design and print files

This is where most delays happen. A visual for a scaffolding banner is not an enlarged poster. It needs its own aspect ratio, a design that works from a distance, and print files of the right quality.

Typical requirements:

- a file in the correct aspect ratio for the specific surface
- sufficient resolution for large-format print
- fonts embedded or converted to outlines
- colours in CMYK, not RGB

We describe the details in [Scaffolding banners: print files, specifications and design](/en/blog/geruestbanner-druckdaten-spezifikationen-gestaltung). If the visual still needs to be developed, start the design in parallel with choosing the site, not afterwards.

## Step 4: Permit

Large-format advertising in Switzerland generally requires a permit. Responsibilities and procedures differ by canton and municipality, and processing times vary too. Some sites already have a permit, such as Riehenring 141 in Basel, where the city has granted one.

Hyde Media handles the permit process for you. Permits can include content conditions. At Riehenring 141, for example, alcohol advertising, political advertising and pornographic content are excluded. So check early whether your visual fits the conditions of the site. More in [Permits for scaffolding advertising in Switzerland](/en/blog/bewilligungen-geruestwerbung-schweiz).

## Step 5: Print

Large-format banners are printed on special materials, for scaffolding often on mesh, a fabric that lets air through. For very large surfaces, several panels are joined together. Hyde Media handles the print and schedules production around the installation date.

## Step 6: Installation

Installation is coordinated with the scaffolding contractor or the property and depends on the weather: in strong winds it is postponed. Hyde Media takes care of installation and, at the end of the campaign, removal.

## The three most common delays

**1. The visual is not ready.** By far the most common cause. Start the design in parallel with site selection.

**2. The print files are wrong.** Low resolution, RGB colours or the wrong aspect ratio lead to correction rounds. Ask for the specifications as soon as the agreement is in place.

**3. The decision drags on.** While internal approval is pending, someone else books the surface. Scaffolding periods do not wait.

## When time is tight

If you have a fixed date, such as a trade fair or an opening, work backwards from it and build in a buffer. Nobody fully controls the weather, construction progress or print capacity. For Christmas campaigns, see our article on [planning in Q4](/en/blog/black-week-weihnachten-aussenwerbung-q4).

## Checklist

1. Define goal, audience and period
2. Choose site and format
3. Agree the booking and request specifications
4. Design the visual and deliver print files
5. Permit (handled by Hyde Media)
6. Print and installation (handled by Hyde Media)
7. Prepare measurement

### How long does it take for a scaffolding ad to go up?

It depends on whether the visual and the permit are already in place. It is fastest when the site has a permit and you deliver print-ready files. Plan a buffer anyway.

### Who takes care of print and installation?

Hyde Media handles print, installation, removal and permits. You supply the visual.

### What is the minimum campaign length?

The minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks.

# What Is Outdoor Advertising? A Guide to Out-of-Home Media in Switzerland

Outdoor advertising is advertising that reaches people outside their homes: on scaffolding and facades, on posters and screens, at stops, in stations and on trams. The industry calls it out-of-home, or OOH. The surfaces it runs on are called out-of-home media.

This guide explains how outdoor advertising works, which formats exist in Switzerland and how to choose the right one.

## Why outdoor advertising?

Outdoor advertising cannot be clicked away, skipped or blocked. It sits where people move and is seen by everyone who passes, every day of the campaign. That gives it three strengths:

- **Reach:** a large surface at a busy junction is seen by a great many people every day. At Riehenring 141 in Basel, for example, it is 39'851 contacts per day.
- **Repetition:** people take the same routes every day. They see your message again and again, and that builds recall.
- **Presence and trust:** a brand that is visible in the cityscape feels real and tangible.

Outdoor also makes other channels work harder. Many people see a brand on the street first and look it up online later. More on our page about [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix).

## The main out-of-home media in Switzerland

### Scaffolding advertising

Large-format banners on the scaffolding of buildings under renovation. Scaffolding surfaces are among the largest advertising spaces in a city and are often in places where there is no other advertising. The period follows the construction phase. More under [scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding).

### Facade advertising

Banners on facades and gable walls that stay up for longer. The steady format that builds awareness through repetition. More under [facade advertising](/en/facade).

### Posters

Poster sites on streets, at stations and at stops, in Switzerland often in the classic Swiss "Weltformat". Posters are usually booked as a network across a city, a region or the whole country.

### Digital out-of-home (DOOH)

Screens in public space, for example in stations or shopping centres. You book a share of the airtime and can change the message during the campaign.

### Transit advertising

Advertising on and in trams, buses and trains, and at stations. The message travels through the city, and people waiting at stops have time to look.

Hyde Media specialises in the large formats: scaffolding and facade advertising. See an overview of what we offer under [services](/en/services).

## How do you choose the right format?

Start by asking who you want to reach and how those people move.

- **Launching something and need a lot of attention fast?** A large scaffolding site at a busy junction is the first choice.
- **Want to build awareness over months?** A facade is a better fit.
- **Need broad presence across many neighbourhoods?** A poster network covers many sites.
- **Does your message change often?** Digital screens allow changes without reprinting.

For a detailed comparison of the two large formats, see [Scaffolding vs. facade](/en/blog/geruest-vs-fassade-richtige-wahl).

## What does outdoor advertising cost?

The price depends on site, size, period and production. A large surface at a busy junction costs more than a single poster, but it offers a different kind of visibility. So compare not only the total price but also the price per 1,000 contacts (CPM). At Hyde Media, prices are provided on request. You can calculate the contacts for different campaign periods in the [campaign calculator](/en/kampagnenrechner).

## Does outdoor advertising need a permit?

Large-format advertising in Switzerland generally requires a permit. Who is responsible and which conditions apply differs by canton and municipality. Hyde Media handles the permit process for scaffolding and facade advertising. Our article on [permits for scaffolding advertising in Switzerland](/en/blog/bewilligungen-geruestwerbung-schweiz) gives an overview.

## How to get started

1. Decide who you want to reach, and in which city or neighbourhood.
2. Choose the format based on goal, period and budget.
3. See the available surfaces with size, contacts and period under [Sites](/en/standorte).
4. Allow enough lead time. [From booking to banner](/en/blog/zeitplan-ooh-kampagne-buchung-bis-banner) shows what a realistic timeline looks like.
5. Decide before launch how you will measure success.

The key terms are explained briefly in the [glossary](/en/glossar).

## FAQ

### What is the difference between outdoor advertising and OOH?

There is none. OOH stands for "out-of-home" and is the internationally used term for outdoor advertising, meaning advertising that reaches people outside their homes.

### What types of outdoor advertising are there?

The main formats include scaffolding advertising, facade advertising, posters, digital out-of-home (DOOH) and transit advertising.

### Who is outdoor advertising for?

Brands that want to be visible in a city or region: for launches, openings, seasonal campaigns, employer branding or long-term brand building.

### How long does an outdoor campaign run?

It depends on the format. At Hyde Media the minimum booking for scaffolding and facade advertising is four weeks.

Thinking about getting started with outdoor advertising? [Contact us](/en/contact) and we will show you which surfaces fit your goal.

title: Effective OOH Advertising Strategies for 2026
excerpt: Eight strategies for effective outdoor advertising in Switzerland: from site selection and format to measuring your OOH campaign.
content:
# Effective OOH Advertising Strategies for 2026

Outdoor advertising, also called out-of-home (OOH), is one of the oldest advertising media there is, and one of the few that cannot be clicked away, skipped or blocked. But a free surface alone does not make a campaign work. What matters is the site, the format, the message and the timing.

Here are eight strategies brands can use to plan more effective OOH campaigns in Switzerland in 2026.

## 1. Start with how your audience moves, not with the format

The most common planning mistake is to start by looking for a format. A better question is: where does my audience move every day, and how?

- **Drivers** see a site from a distance and have a few seconds.
- **Tram and bus passengers** move more slowly and often wait at stops.
- **Pedestrians and cyclists** are close by and move at their own pace.

At a traffic-light junction with a tram stop, all three groups come together, and waiting at the lights extends the viewing time. Sites like these are particularly interesting for large-format outdoor advertising.

## 2. Big formats for big moments

For launches, brand campaigns and anything that needs to stand out, large surfaces are hard to beat. [Scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding) uses the scaffolding around buildings under renovation and offers some of the largest advertising spaces in a city. [Facade advertising](/en/facade) puts your brand on a prominent building wall for a longer period.

A big format needs a clear idea, though. One image, few words and a recognisable logo work better across a hundred square metres than a list of offers.

## 3. Plan for repetition

Outdoor advertising works through repetition. People take the same routes to work, to the shops and back home every day. A brand that is present at a well-chosen site for several weeks is seen by the same people again and again. That is why the minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks.

## 4. Simplify the message radically

Nobody in traffic has time for small print. What works:

- one central statement in as few words as possible,
- strong contrast between text and background,
- a logo that can be recognised from far away,
- a single strong image rather than several small ones.

Read more in our [creative best practices for outdoor advertising](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung).

## 5. Connect offline and online

Outdoor and digital channels complement each other. People who see a brand in the city often search for it online later. So plan your search and social campaigns to run at the same time and use the same visual. A short web address or a QR code can make sense where people stand still, such as at a tram stop. Our page on [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix) shows how outdoor fits into the wider plan.

## 6. Use the city's calendar

Every city has its own rhythm. In Basel, trade fairs and congresses around Messe Basel and the Congress Center Basel shape the year, alongside major cultural events, the autumn fair and the Advent season. Aligning your campaign with dates like these lets you reach additional audiences, such as trade visitors from Switzerland and abroad. For the Christmas season, see our article on [planning outdoor advertising in Q4](/en/blog/black-week-weihnachten-aussenwerbung-q4).

## 7. Think about sustainability

Large-format banners are a physical product. Ask about material, production and disposal when you plan, and design visuals that stay relevant for the whole campaign period. A timeless brand message does not need to be replaced halfway through.

## 8. Measure what can be measured

Outdoor advertising has no clicks, but it can still be evaluated. Traffic figures show how many contacts a site offers. Impact is measured through brand awareness, searches for your brand, website visits and visits to nearby stores. We explain how in [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen). You can compare the reach of different sites and periods in the [campaign calculator](/en/kampagnenrechner).

## Conclusion

Effective outdoor advertising starts with where and how your audience moves. A well-chosen site, a format with presence, a simple message and enough time for repetition are the foundation. Timing, integration with digital channels and clean measurement do the rest.

## FAQ

### What is the most important strategy in outdoor advertising?

The site. A surface only works if your audience actually passes it. Check traffic flow, visibility and surroundings first, and choose format and visual after that.

### How long should an OOH campaign run?

Long enough for the same people to see your message several times. At Hyde Media the minimum booking is four weeks. For brand building, longer periods make sense.

### Is outdoor advertising worth it alongside digital marketing?

Yes, the channels complement each other. Outdoor creates visibility in everyday life, and digital channels capture the interest when people search for your brand later.

# Scaffolding vs. Facade: Which Format is Right for Your Campaign?

Scaffolding and facade advertising are among the largest advertising surfaces a city has to offer. Both put your brand on a building in large format, both are visible from a distance, and Hyde Media handles both from start to finish: print, installation, removal and permits. Even so, they suit different goals.

Here is how the two formats differ, and how to choose the right one.

## What is scaffolding advertising?

With [scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding), a large-format banner is mounted on the scaffolding around a building that is being renovated. The surface only exists while the scaffolding is up. For property owners it is a way to refinance part of the building works. For advertisers it is a chance to get a space in places where advertising would otherwise not be possible.

**Strengths of scaffolding advertising:**

- **Very large surfaces**, often well over a hundred square metres.
- **Surprise effect**: the space is new in the cityscape and gets noticed.
- **Central locations**: renovations happen everywhere, including places without traditional advertising sites.
- **Ideal for launches** and campaigns that need a lot of attention in a short time.

**What to keep in mind:** the period follows the construction phase. Good scaffolding sites are booked quickly, and your campaign start has to fit the building schedule.

## What is facade advertising?

With [facade advertising](/en/facade), a banner is fixed directly to a building's facade or gable wall, independent of any building works. That makes the space easier to plan and well suited to longer periods.

**Strengths of facade advertising:**

- **Longer presence**: you stay in the cityscape for months.
- **Predictability**: the period does not depend on a construction project.
- **Brand building through repetition**: the same people see your message day after day.

**What to keep in mind:** facade advertising relies on consistency. The visual should still be relevant after several weeks.

## The differences at a glance

- **Duration:** scaffolding advertising follows the construction phase; facade advertising suits longer, predictable periods. For both formats, the minimum booking at Hyde Media is four weeks.
- **Impact:** scaffolding creates a strong, eye-catching accent. A facade builds awareness over time.
- **Flexibility:** with scaffolding, availability decides the start date. With a facade you have more room to plan.
- **Typical uses:** scaffolding for launches, seasonal promotions and events. Facades for brand building, local presence and employer branding.
- **Price:** for both formats the price depends on site, size, period and production. Hyde Media provides a quote on request.

## Which format fits your goal?

**Launching a product or opening a location?** Then attention in a short time is what counts. A large scaffolding site at a busy junction is the first choice. One example is the «Sparkling Life» campaign by [Grand Casino Basel at Riehenring 141](/en/cases/grand-casino-basel-riehenring), where two banners cover both street faces of a corner building.

**Want to anchor your brand in a city for the long term?** Then continuity matters more than surprise. A facade accompanies your audience for months.

**Working towards a fixed date, such as a trade fair?** Check early which sites are free in that period. With scaffolding, the building works set the calendar, not the media plan.

## Combine both formats

The strongest campaigns often use both. A facade provides a steady base presence, and a scaffolding site adds a highly visible accent during a launch or promotion. That way you combine awareness with activation.

## FAQ

### What is the difference between scaffolding and facade advertising?

Scaffolding advertising is mounted on construction scaffolding and is tied to the duration of the works. Facade advertising hangs directly on a building wall and suits longer, predictable periods.

### Which format is cheaper?

There is no general answer. For both formats the price depends on site, size, period and production. Hyde Media will prepare an individual quote.

### Do I need a permit?

Large-format advertising on buildings generally requires a permit, and the rules differ by canton and municipality. Hyde Media handles the permit process for you. Read more in our article on [permits for scaffolding advertising](/en/blog/bewilligungen-geruestwerbung-schweiz).

Not sure which format fits your campaign? [Contact us](/en/contact) and we will suggest suitable sites.

# Outdoor Advertising in Zurich: The Key Areas for OOH Campaigns

Zurich is Switzerland's largest city and the country's economic centre. Every day, commuters from the whole region come into the city, along with business travellers, students and tourists. That makes Zurich an obvious market for outdoor advertising, but also one with a lot of competition for attention.

Here is an overview of the areas that matter most for out-of-home (OOH) in Zurich, and of how to evaluate a site.

## Main station and Europaallee

Zurich main station is one of the country's most important transport hubs. Long-distance trains, S-Bahn, trams and buses all meet around it. The Europaallee next to it has grown into a district of offices, shops and restaurants. Here you reach a broad, mobile audience, from commuters to business travellers.

## City centre and Bahnhofstrasse

The city centre with Bahnhofstrasse is Switzerland's best-known shopping street. Much of the audience is on foot and has time to look. The centre is attractive for premium brands, retail and restaurants. As in any historic centre, however, large formats are particularly sensitive here in terms of design and permits.

## Zurich West and Hardbrücke

The former industrial area of Zurich West has become a district for work, living, culture and nightlife. The Hardbrücke, a major traffic artery, and Hardbrücke station keep a lot of people on the move. For brands that want to reach a young, urban, working audience, this area is interesting.

## Districts 4 and 5

Around Langstrasse and in districts 4 and 5, the city is dense, lively and mixed. Many people live, work and go out in a small area. Large-format advertising on scaffolding stands out particularly well in these densely built neighbourhoods, because there are few traditional advertising sites.

## Oerlikon

Oerlikon in the north of the city is a centre in its own right, with a major station, residential and office districts, and venues such as the Hallenstadion and Messe Zürich. On event days, additional audiences come into the area.

## Seefeld, Bellevue and the lakeside

Around Bellevue and along the lakeside, many people are on the move on foot, by tram and by car, especially in good weather and at weekends. Here you meet locals and tourists alike.

## Main traffic arteries

The major routes into the city take many drivers past the same places every day. For large scaffolding and facade surfaces these routes are particularly valuable, because the surfaces are seen from a distance and from several directions. The message has to be short and large, though.

## How to evaluate a site in Zurich

Whatever the neighbourhood, these questions help you compare surfaces.

- **How many people pass?** Ask for the contacts per day and scale them up to the campaign period. Our article on [calculating the reach of an outdoor campaign](/en/blog/reichweite-aussenwerbung-berechnen) shows how.
- **How do they move?** On foot, by tram, by bike or by car? That decides how much text your message can carry.
- **How visible is the surface?** From one direction or several, head-on or at an angle?
- **How long does the gaze linger?** Traffic lights, stops and pedestrian zones extend dwell time.
- **Do the surroundings fit?** A site in an office district reaches a different audience from one in a nightlife area.

## Competition for attention

In Zurich many brands compete for attention. That makes a clear, simple message and a format that stands out from its surroundings all the more important. Large-format scaffolding advertising has an advantage here: it is new in the cityscape and much larger than most other surfaces. See our [creative best practices](/en/blog/kreative-best-practices-aussenwerbung) for design tips.

## Zurich or Basel?

Whether Zurich, Basel or both make sense for your campaign depends on your audience. See our comparison [Basel vs. Zurich: where should you advertise?](/en/blog/basel-vs-zuerich-aussenwerbung). You will find the currently available Hyde Media surfaces under [Sites](/en/standorte).

## FAQ

### Where is outdoor advertising most effective in Zurich?

Around the major transport hubs such as the main station, on the main traffic arteries and in busy neighbourhoods. What matters is that your audience passes regularly.

### Does scaffolding advertising in Zurich need a permit?

Large-format advertising in Swiss cities generally requires a permit, and the rules differ by canton and municipality. Hyde Media handles the permit process. Read more in [permits for scaffolding advertising in Switzerland](/en/blog/bewilligungen-geruestwerbung-schweiz).

### How long should a campaign in Zurich run?

Long enough for your audience to see the message several times. At Hyde Media the minimum booking is four weeks.

Planning a campaign in German-speaking Switzerland? [Contact us](/en/contact) and we will advise you on suitable surfaces.

Basel SBB is the gateway to the city for commuters from the whole region and for travellers from Switzerland and abroad. Around the station, people move on foot, by tram and by car. For brands that want to reach a broad, mobile audience, the station area is a natural candidate.

Between Marktplatz, Barfüsserplatz and the shopping streets, much of the audience is on foot. People are close to the surfaces and have time to look. The centre is attractive for retail, restaurants and anything that should prompt a visit. Large-format advertising is particularly sensitive here because of the historic townscape, both in terms of design and permits.

## Tram junctions in the neighbourhoods

Many of the most effective surfaces are not in the centre but at major tram junctions in the neighbourhoods. Trams stop, cars wait at the lights, and cyclists and pedestrians cross. One example is the campaign by [EVO Fitness at Burgfelderstrasse 1](/en/cases/evo-fitness-basel-burgfelderstrasse), where a corner position covered two street faces at once.

## What matters when choosing a site

- **Traffic flow:** how many people pass, and how? Drivers need large, simple messages; pedestrians can read more.
- **Visibility:** can the surface be seen from several directions? Corner buildings at junctions are especially valuable.
- **Dwell time:** at traffic lights and stops, people have more time to look.
- **Surroundings:** does the site fit your audience, such as fair visitors, commuters or local residents?
- **Timing:** is the surface available when your campaign needs to run?

## Seasonal highlights in Basel

Basel has a busy events calendar. Trade fairs and congresses bring visitors from around the world, the autumn fair and the Christmas market fill the city centre in the second half of the year, and Fasnacht shapes the city in spring. Aligning your campaign with dates like these brings additional audiences.

## The tri-border area as an advantage

Because of its location on the border, many people commute into Basel from France and Germany. A campaign in Basel therefore reaches not just city residents but a tri-national audience. Make sure your message works without much text, so it carries across language borders.

## FAQ

### Where is outdoor advertising most effective in Basel?

Wherever your audience passes every day and the surface is clearly visible. Major junctions with tram lines, the routes around Messe Basel and the approaches from the motorway are among the strongest locations.

title: How to Measure Your OOH Campaign Success
excerpt: Contacts, reach, brand awareness and search: the metrics that show whether your outdoor advertising works, and how to collect them.
content:
# How to Measure Your OOH Campaign Success

Outdoor advertising has no clicks and no cookies. Even so, it is quite possible to judge whether a campaign has worked. The key is to decide before launch what the campaign should achieve, and to choose the right metrics for it.

Here are the metrics available and how to collect them.

## Step 1: Set the goal

A brand awareness campaign is measured differently from a promotion meant to drive store visits. Typical goals are:

- **Awareness**: more people should know your brand.
- **Image**: your brand should be perceived differently or more strongly.
- **Activation**: people should do something, such as visit a website, sign up or come by.

Choose one main goal and two or three metrics to go with it. Trying to measure everything usually means measuring nothing properly.

## Step 2: Understand the media metrics

These metrics describe how many people could see your campaign.

- **Contacts (OTS, opportunity to see):** the number of opportunities to see the ad. Someone who passes five times counts five times.
- **Reach:** the number of different people who saw the campaign at least once.
- **Frequency:** how often one person saw the campaign on average. Reach times frequency gives the contacts.
- **CPM (cost per thousand):** the cost per 1,000 contacts. It lets you compare sites and media on a common basis.

For every Hyde Media site we provide the contacts per day. Our article on [calculating the reach of an outdoor campaign](/en/blog/reichweite-aussenwerbung-berechnen) shows how to turn that into the contacts for a whole campaign. The terms are also explained in the [glossary](/en/glossar).

## Step 3: Measure the impact

Contacts show the potential. Whether the campaign worked, you measure with these methods:

### Surveys before and after

A short survey in the target region before launch and towards the end of the campaign shows whether awareness, recall or image have changed. Ask the same questions both times.

### Searches for your brand

Many people look a brand up online after seeing it in the city. Compare searches for your brand name in the region during the campaign with a period before it.

### Website visits and direct traffic

Watch direct traffic and visits from the campaign region. A dedicated short landing page, promoted only on the outdoor ad, makes the effect easier to see.

### QR codes and promo codes

Where people stand still, such as at a tram stop, a QR code can make sense. A promo code that appears only on the banner shows how many customers come via the campaign. One example is the campaign by [EVO Fitness in Basel](/en/cases/evo-fitness-basel-burgfelderstrasse), where a QR code on both sides of the banner led straight to sign-up.

### Store visits

If your store is near the site, compare footfall or sales with a period without the campaign.

## Step 4: Create a comparison

Impact is easiest to show when you have something to compare with:

- **Before and after:** the same metrics before, during and after the campaign.
- **Test and control area:** the campaign runs in one city but not in a comparable one. The difference shows the effect.

Make sure as little else as possible differs between the periods or areas, such as price promotions or other campaigns.

## Common mistakes

- **Looking only at contacts:** contacts show how many people could see the campaign, not whether it worked.
- **Starting too late:** if you only think about measurement after the campaign, you have no baseline.
- **Last-click thinking:** outdoor often works indirectly. Counting only the last click underestimates its contribution.

Read more about how outdoor supports other channels in [OOH in the media mix](/en/ooh-im-medienmix).

## FAQ

### How do you measure the success of outdoor advertising?

With a combination of media metrics such as contacts and reach, and impact metrics such as brand awareness, searches, website visits and store visits. Set a goal and a baseline before launch.

### What does OTS mean?

OTS stands for "opportunity to see". The figure is gross: someone who passes several times is counted several times.

### Is a QR code on a scaffolding banner worth it?

Mainly where people stand still, such as at a stop or traffic lights. In moving traffic, a short, memorable web address often works better.

# Basel vs. Zurich: Where Should You Advertise?

Basel and Zurich are among the most important markets for outdoor advertising in German-speaking Switzerland. Both are economically strong, well connected and have dense tram networks. Even so, they differ clearly, and the right choice depends on who you want to reach.

Here is a comparison of the two cities from an out-of-home planning perspective.

## Zurich: the largest market

Zurich is Switzerland's largest city and the country's economic centre.

- **A large, diverse audience:** commuters from the whole region, professionals in finance and services, students and tourists.
- **A major transport hub:** the main station is one of the central nodes in the Swiss rail network.
- **Plenty of competition:** many brands advertise in Zurich. To stand out you need a strong format and a clear message.

For an overview of the key areas, see [Outdoor advertising in Zurich](/en/blog/zuerich-standorte-aussenwerbung).

## Basel: compact, international, a trade fair city

Basel is smaller than Zurich but has a distinctive profile.

- **The tri-border area:** the city borders Germany and France, and many people commute into Basel from the neighbouring countries. A campaign reaches a tri-national audience.
- **A trade fair and congress city:** trade visitors from Switzerland and abroad regularly gather around Messe Basel and the Congress Center Basel.
- **Life sciences and culture:** Basel is a major centre of the pharma and life sciences industry and has a rich cultural scene.
- **Short distances:** trams, cars, cyclists and pedestrians cross paths in a small area. Well-chosen sites therefore reach many different groups.

Hyde Media is based in Basel. At [Riehenring 141](/en/standorte/riehenring-141), right next to Messe Basel, our 175 m² scaffolding site delivers 39'851 contacts per day. Read more about Basel's locations in [Top locations for outdoor advertising in Basel](/en/blog/basel-standorte-aussenwerbung).

## The comparison by criteria

### Reach

As the largest city, Zurich offers a larger potential audience. For the reach of a single surface, though, what matters is not the size of the city but the traffic at the specific site. A surface at a busy junction in Basel can deliver more contacts than one on a quiet side street in Zurich.

### Attention

Fewer campaigns compete for attention in Basel than in Zurich, so a large-format banner stands out more. In Zurich competition is greater, and the demands on format and creative are higher.

### Audience

- **Finance and services, a national audience:** Zurich.
- **Trade fair visitors, life sciences, a cross-border audience:** Basel.
- **A broad urban audience:** both cities.

### Timing

Both cities have their own events calendars. In Basel the year is shaped by trade fairs, congresses, the autumn fair, Fasnacht and the Advent season. If you want to reach trade visitors, plan your campaign around the fair dates.

## Which city fits your campaign?

**Choose Zurich** if you are building a national brand, want the largest possible audience and your target group is strongly rooted in finance and services.

**Choose Basel** if you want to reach trade fair and congress visitors, your audience is cross-border, or you want to stand out with a large format in a less cluttered environment.

**Choose both** if you want broad presence in German-speaking Switzerland. A shared visual in both cities strengthens recognition.

## Our recommendation

Start where your audience is strongest, and measure the impact. Then expand the campaign in a targeted way. Read how to measure impact in [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen).

## FAQ

### Is outdoor advertising more effective in Basel or in Zurich?

It depends on the site and your audience, not on the city alone. What matters is the contacts at the specific site, its visibility and its surroundings.

### What is special about Basel for outdoor advertising?

Its location in the tri-border area with commuters from Germany and France, Messe Basel with its international trade audience, and the short distances where many traffic flows cross.

### Can I run a campaign in both cities at the same time?

Yes. A shared visual in both cities strengthens recognition. Make sure the campaign periods are aligned.

# Outdoor Advertising in Switzerland: A Guide for Brands

Switzerland is a distinctive market for outdoor advertising. The country is small but diverse: several national languages, strong cities with their own character, and a federal system in which cantons and municipalities regulate a great deal themselves. To succeed with out-of-home (OOH) here, you need to know these particularities.

This guide gives you an overview.

## What makes Switzerland different

### Several language regions

German, French, Italian and Romansh are national languages. A campaign meant to run nationally therefore often needs several language versions. Even within one region it pays to look at the audience: in Basel, for example, many people commute in from France and Germany. Strong visuals with little text work best across language borders.

### Federalism and local rules

Advertising is subject not only to federal law but also to cantonal and municipal rules. Who is responsible, and which conditions apply, differs from canton to canton and municipality to municipality. For advertisers this means: plan for permits, or work with a partner who handles them. For scaffolding and facade advertising, Hyde Media takes care of the entire permit process. We give an overview in our article on [permits for scaffolding advertising in Switzerland](/en/blog/bewilligungen-geruestwerbung-schweiz).

### Strong cities with their own profile

Zurich is the country's largest city and its economic centre. Geneva has an international character, Bern is the federal city, and Basel combines trade fairs, life sciences and culture in the tri-border area. Each city has its own audience and its own traffic flows. For a direct comparison of two markets, see [Basel vs. Zurich](/en/blog/basel-vs-zuerich-aussenwerbung).

## The main OOH formats in Switzerland

- **Posters:** classic poster sites on streets, at stations and at stops, usually booked as a network across a city or region.
- **Digital out-of-home (DOOH):** screens in public space where you book a share of the airtime.
- **Transit advertising:** advertising on and in trams, buses and trains, and at stations.
- **Scaffolding advertising:** large-format banners on the scaffolding of buildings under renovation. More under [scaffolding advertising](/en/scaffolding).
- **Facade advertising:** banners on facades and gable walls for longer periods. More under [facade advertising](/en/facade).

Hyde Media specialises in the large formats: scaffolding and facade advertising, based in Basel. You will find our current surfaces under [Sites](/en/standorte).

## Planning in five steps

### 1. Define audience and region

Who do you want to reach, and where does that audience move? A national campaign needs different planning from a campaign for a single city or neighbourhood.

### 2. Choose the format for the goal

For a launch that needs a lot of attention quickly, a large scaffolding site is a good fit. For brand building over months, a facade. For broad coverage, a poster network. Many campaigns combine several formats.

### 3. Evaluate the sites

Look at contacts per day, visibility from different directions, dwell time at traffic lights and stops, and the surroundings. With the [campaign calculator](/en/kampagnenrechner) you can calculate the contacts for different campaign lengths.

### 4. Draw up a timeline

Work backwards from your start date: site selection, contract, design, print files, a permit where needed, print and installation. We describe the process in detail in [From booking to banner](/en/blog/zeitplan-ooh-kampagne-buchung-bis-banner).

### 5. Measure success

Decide before launch how you will measure success. See [How to measure your OOH campaign success](/en/blog/ooh-kampagnenerfolg-messen) for tips.

## Recommendation: start with one city

If you are working with large-format outdoor advertising for the first time, start in one city with a clear goal. You will learn which sites and messages work, and can then expand to other cities in a targeted way.

## FAQ

### How much does outdoor advertising cost in Switzerland?

It depends on format, site, size, period and production. At Hyde Media, prices are provided on request and tailored to your campaign.

### Does outdoor advertising in Switzerland need a permit?

Large-format advertising generally requires a permit. Responsibilities and conditions differ by canton and municipality. Hyde Media handles the application for you.

### Which language should I advertise in?

In the language of the region where the campaign runs. In Basel that is German, although part of the audience comes from France and Germany. Strong visuals with little text work across language borders.

Planning a campaign in Switzerland? [Contact us](/en/contact) and we will advise you on format, site and timing.

title: Creative Best Practices for Outdoor Advertising
excerpt: Few words, strong contrast, one big image: design rules that make your scaffolding or facade advertising work from a distance.
content:
# Creative Best Practices for Outdoor Advertising

In outdoor advertising, the design decides within seconds whether a message lands. People drive past, wait briefly at the lights or glance out of the tram. They have no time to read and no reason to make an effort. Good creative makes it easy for them.

Here are the key design rules for large-format outdoor advertising such as scaffolding and facade banners.

## 1. One message, not three

The most important rule: focus on a single statement. What should someone take away from a quick glance at the surface? Anything that does not support that statement does not belong on the banner.

A well-known industry rule of thumb is to use as few words as possible, ideally no more than a handful. The greater the distance and the faster the traffic, the shorter the text needs to be.

## 2. Contrast before aesthetics

A design that looks elegant on screen can disappear on the street. Make sure there is strong contrast between text and background. Light text on a dark background, or the other way round, is almost always more legible than tone-on-tone. Consider the surroundings too: a facade, trees or the sky behind the banner all affect how it reads.

## 3. Typography for distance

- **Bold, clear typefaces** are easier to read than thin or decorative ones.
- **Large type sizes**: what looks big in the draft is often small from fifty metres away.
- **Few lines**: one or two lines are ideal.
- **No blocks of capitals**: longer text in capitals is harder to read.

## 4. One strong image

A single, expressive image works better than a collage. People, faces and products in close-up draw the eye. Make sure the image still makes sense when heavily reduced, because that is how the audience sees it from a distance.

## 5. Make the logo bigger than you think

If people remember only one thing, it should be your brand. Place the logo where it is clearly visible and large enough to be recognised from afar. On very large formats it pays to keep the logo and the key message close together.

## 6. Choose colours carefully

Colours carry mood and brand identity. In the cityscape your banner competes with many other impressions. Strong, clear colours that fit your brand stand out better than pastels. Keep in mind that mesh material makes colours look slightly lighter.

## 7. Think about the site

Every surface is seen differently. A banner on a corner building is visible from two directions; a site on an arterial road is often seen at an angle from a moving car. Before designing, ask how your audience sees the surface. In the campaign by [Grand Casino Basel at Riehenring 141](/en/cases/grand-casino-basel-riehenring), two banners cover both street faces so the visual works from every direction of travel.

## 8. Speak locally

A reference to the city or neighbourhood creates closeness. It can be a place name, a pointer to the nearest store or a visual that connects to the surroundings. In Basel, where commuters from France and Germany are also on the move, it pays to keep the message as visual as possible.

## 9. Test before printing

Test your design before it goes to print:

- **The phone test:** look at the draft small on your phone. If it is not legible there, it will not be legible on the street.
- **The three-second test:** show the draft to someone for three seconds. Can they say who the ad is from and what it is about?
- **The distance test:** print the draft small and look at it from a few metres away.

We explain the technical requirements for artwork in [Scaffolding banners: print files, specifications and design](/en/blog/geruestbanner-druckdaten-spezifikationen-gestaltung).

## FAQ

### How much text belongs on a scaffolding banner?

As little as possible. A short key message, the logo and perhaps a short web address are enough. Anything more distracts.

### Can I use an existing poster design?

Often yes, but it needs to be adapted to the format. Large-format banners have different proportions, and small details get lost at a distance.

### Does Hyde Media design the visual?

Hyde Media handles print, installation, removal and permits. We are happy to advise on how your visual will work on a given site.

Have a visual and looking for the right surface? [Contact us](/en/contact).
